text: No. It runs none of an app's code (checked: appServer.js serves <app>.html and <app>.js as files and never executes them). It hands a browser one app's files and passes two fixed verbs back to its owner, the way a screen shows what it's given. It serves apps no more than the relay does. The shell is what runs apps. So faceServer is the honest name.

wsl-claude: close to precise, not quite. What I could write tests for today:
DECIDED: a faceless process on your node; reached only by your node over its pipe; members find it through 'api' ({description, request, reply}); access needs your contact list plus grantFace's own list; a grant writes the name AND syncs the face's contacts by owner command; freeing a name removes both; the member's client stores its grants (several providers) and adds the face key taken from your node's signed answer.
STILL OPEN, each one line from you or the lead:
1) HOW YOUR NODE STARTS IT. 'serves: true' now means a face server, and you ruled grantFace is not one. So what does its manifest say, and what starts it?
2) WHO OWNS grants.json. Today appFaceApp owns it and answers the face's route questions from it. If grantFace takes it over, appFaceApp (a booted app that sees only its own folder) can't read it. One owner, and a way for the other to ask.
3) HOW IT REACHES THE OWNER COMMAND. A process has no door address today (claude-windows' two prerequisite fixes).
4) 'peer' FOR THE FACE. The sync needs acquire before accept: carry ['contact','peer'] on the face, or not.
5) WHERE THE MEMBER'S CLIENT RUNS (a process like grantFace, or a booted app) and how it adds a contact on its own node.

taking team/chat (a precise enough picture of grantFace?). Also, from the rename: your face-vocabulary check in faceLastLeg split on \n, so on a Windows checkout the trailing \r stopped the comment strip, and /face/ matched 'interface'. I fixed it to split on /\r?\n/ with /\bface/ (in the rename commit).

Thanks for the \r catch. One problem with /\bface/: it misses camelCase. 'readFaces' has no word boundary before F, so the exact function your split removed would slip back in unnoticed. Checked: /\bface/i is false for readFaces. Please use this in your rename commit instead, to avoid us both editing the same lines: split on /\r?\n/, strip comments, then code.replace(/\b(inter|sur)face/gi, '') and test /face/i. That catches readFaces, faceTable and faceNameOf, and passes interface and surface.

Close to precise. What's SETTLED for grantFace:
- WHAT: a faceless app on your box, running as its own process, that takes grant requests, keeps the name table, and keeps each face's contacts in step by owner command. Fully automatic.
- VERBS it describes of itself: grant { name } gives the granted name; faceKey gives the face's key to trust. Each verb is { description, request, reply }.
- IN: only from members in your contacts and on grantFace's allow list, forwarded by your node down its pipe. OUT: back through your node, signed with your key.
- TABLE: keyed by face domain plus name. route? and serve move in from appFaceApp.
- CLIENT on the member's side: stores its grants keyed by face plus name, acquires then accepts the face's key, and answers 'under construction' with no handler.
STILL OPEN, and it's blocking: the floor under it. An app process can't run its own code yet (faceServer runs none). So the first decision is how grantFace's own code runs: its own server module, loaded by the process your node starts, with a spirit object that reaches the door.
Go! = I write that floor up as the design, then build bottom up.
